MUQATIL:92:7-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:92:7-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:92:7-15/r1.claim: God makes the generous person inclined to give again and eases that person toward good.

FARRA:v3p270/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p270/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p270/r5.claim: Being made easy for the easier path means being enabled to return to righteous action.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#3/r1.claim: Being made easy for the easier path means being enabled to return to righteous action.

TUSTARI:92:7/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:7/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:7/r1.claim: The easy path is a return to goodness.

TAB:92:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:7/r1.claim: God prepares the generous, God-fearing believer for the easy course: pleasing deeds in this world that earn Paradise in the next.

TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.claim: Al-Tabari contrasts the easier course of obedience prepared for the giver with the miser who withholds the bounty given by God and considers himself independent of his Lord.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the giver fears his Lord, believes in God's promised recompense, and is eased toward good by God.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the easy path as Paradise.

THALABI:v10p217/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p217/r5.claim: Yassiruhu means God will prepare the person in worldly life; al-yusra is the easy path of acting as God approves.

THALABI:v10p217/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p217/r6.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about Abu Bakr.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r26.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r26.claim: Ibn Abbas says God will ease the person toward good.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r27.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r27.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the destination is Paradise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r28.claim: Mawardi allows that God will make the means of goodness and righteousness easy for the person.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.claim: Qatada reports from Khulayd, from Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet said two angels call each sunrise for God to replace the spender's gift and ruin the hoarder's wealth, then recited these verses; no grading is stated.

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r8.claim: God makes obedience easy, disobedience hateful, nearness desirable, faith beloved, and excellence attractive to the heart.

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r9.claim: Another explanation is continuing in God's obedience and returning to acts of worship already performed.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s instruction to act rather than rely on one’s recorded destiny, since each is facilitated toward what he was created for; he then recited these verses.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports that Abū Bakr’s father urged him to free strong slaves who could protect him, but Abū Bakr said he sought another purpose; the verses were revealed concerning him and his father’s advice.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p79/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p79/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p79/r1.claim: God will prepare the person for good works; Ibn Abbas similarly says that good deeds will be made easy for him.

WAHIDI-QT:92:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:7/r1.claim: God prepares him for the easy course of deeds that please God.

WAHIDI-QT:92:7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:7/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:7/r2.claim: Abu Bakr bought a group of people whom the polytheists tortured in an effort to make them renounce Islam; God described him as generous and believing in divine recompense.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r5.claim: God prepares the easy course of deeds pleasing to Him; Abū Bakr exemplified it by buying and freeing people tortured to make them renounce Islam, in confidence of God's reward.

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r7.claim: Al-yusrā is the feminine form of “easier”; yusr means comfort and abundance, while taysīr means easing or lightening a matter.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r1.claim: God prepares the giver for the easier course: actions that He approves.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.claim: The Prophet says every soul has a written place in Paradise or Hell, but people must still act: each is eased toward the deeds for which they were created.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.claim: Ata reports an Ansari’s palm dropped dates into a neighbor’s yard. After its owner refused the Prophet’s Paradise-palm offer, Abu al-Dahdah traded his orchard for it; the Prophet gave the tree to the neighbor, and the revelation contrasts their efforts.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r1.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r1.claim: An Ansari’s palm dropped dates into a neighbor’s yard for his children; when its owner refused the Prophet’s offer of a palm in Paradise, Abu al-Dahdah traded his orchard for the tree. The Prophet accepted and gave the tree to the neighbor; the revelation refers to their different efforts.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: In this story, the giver is Abu al-Dahdah, the promised good is reward, and the easier path is Paradise; the miser is the Ansari, who denies reward and is eased toward Hell.

KASHSHAF:92:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:7/r1.claim: Yusirr means to prepare someone, by analogy with making a horse ready for riding by saddling and bridling it.

KASHSHAF:92:7/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:7/r2.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF:92:7/r2.claim: The Prophet says each person is facilitated toward what he was created for.

KASHSHAF:92:7/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:7/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:7/r3.claim: God will gently guide and enable the person until obedience becomes easiest, as when God opens someone's heart to Islam.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.claim: We will ease him toward ease means preparing him for it, as a horse is saddled and bridled, and guiding him until obedience becomes easy; compare the promise to open one's heart to Islam.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says each person is facilitated toward the purpose for which he was created.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r1.claim: Al-yusra is a good, pleasing condition in this life and the next; al-usra is a bad condition in both.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r11.claim: God gradually leads the giver through good works toward ease, an outcome already known to Him.

TABRISI:92:5-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r8.claim: God repeatedly makes obedience easy, preparing and enabling the person to undertake it eagerly and gladly.

TABRISI:92:5-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r9.claim: Yusrā may instead mean the easy state of entering Paradise and receiving the angels' greeting and good news.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p149/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p149/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar vocalizes the sīn of both al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā with ḍamma.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p149/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p149/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p149/r2.claim: Al-yusrā means the good, which God makes easy for the giver.

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.claim: Al-yusra can mean Paradise, goodness, ease in all required acts and omissions, or renewed return to obedience; al-usra can mean shirk, hardship, or returning to withholding financial rights. Al-Qaffal explains both by their outcomes: obedience yields ease and sin hardship.

RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.claim: The feminine ending may refer to a group of deeds, a feminine noun such as khilla or faʿla, the return to a prior act, or a feminine 'way'; it may also call Paradise easy because its promise makes difficult worship feel easy.

RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r3.claim: If yusra means Paradise, making it easy means granting honored entry, as 13:23-24, 39:73 and 13:24 describe.

RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r4.claim: If yusra means good deeds, ease means energizing the person to perform them without the sluggishness of hypocrites, as 2:45, 4:142 and 9:38 illustrate.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r15.claim: God makes the person follow the causes of goodness and soundness until good deeds become easy.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.claim: At a funeral in Baqiʿ, the Prophet says each soul's destination is written, but people must act; each person is made ready for the work of the blessed or wretched, then he recites these verses.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's wording is graded hasan sahih; the Prophet repeats that everyone is made easy for the work for which they were created.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.speaker: غلامان شابان عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow prior decrees or begin anew; the Prophet says decrees, then tells them to act because each is enabled for the work assigned to him.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.speaker: الغلامان
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.claim: After hearing that each is made easy for the work for which he was created, the young men say they will strive and work.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r6.claim: God prepares that person for an easy trait leading to ease and rest, such as entry to Paradise; the verb evokes preparing a horse with saddle and bridle.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#8/r1.claim: God will ease him toward the easy disposition: acting in ways that please his Lord.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r1.claim: God prepares the giver and God-fearer for the easier state in this life and the next; this contrasts giving with stinginess and piety with self-sufficiency.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God withholds favors so obedience becomes hardest, or that the easy and difficult are the paths to Paradise and Hell.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.claim: The author calls a Muʿtazilite implication in al-Zamakhsharī's account and says taysīr can mean preparation for either outcome by way of contrast.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets being facilitated toward ease as being guided to good; Zayd ibn Aslam says it means Paradise.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r2.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r2.claim: Some early authorities say good deeds lead to further good deeds, while sins bring further sins.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.claim: Many verses and reports show God grants success to whoever intends good and abandons whoever intends evil, while all occurs by a determined decree.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.claim: When Abu Bakr asks whether deeds follow a settled decree or a new decision, the Prophet replies that each person is made ready for what he was created to do.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.claim: The Prophet says each persons place in Paradise or Hell and status as fortunate or wretched have been written, prompting the question whether people should then rely on fate.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.claim: In a fuller version, the Prophet says the fortunate are enabled toward fortunate deeds and the wretched toward wretched deeds, then recites the two paths.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.claim: Umar asks whether human deeds are already decreed; the Prophet says each person is facilitated, with the fortunate working toward happiness and the wretched toward misery. Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.claim: Jabir asks whether deeds concern a settled matter or a new one; the Prophet says the matter is settled, and tells Suraqah that every worker is facilitated for his work.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.claim: Muslim also transmits the report in which the Prophet says every worker is facilitated for the work for which he was created.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow what is written; the Prophet says to act, since everyone is facilitated for the work he was created to do.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.claim: The Prophet tells Abu al-Darda that each person is prepared for what he was created for; Ibn Kathir says Ahmad alone transmits this route.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.claim: A report cited by Ibn Jarir says the verses concern Abu Bakr, who freed vulnerable women and elderly converts in Mecca to seek God's reward despite his father's advice to free stronger men for protection.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r3.claim: God prepares the truthful giver for the easy path through mercy, enabling pleasing conduct, a good life, and entry into Paradise; obedience itself can feel burdensome to the self.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.claim: The Prophet’s maxim says each person is made easy for the path for which he was created, supporting the prior decree of each outcome.

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.claim: He reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God; the verses contrast their efforts with those of Umayya and Ubayy, identify the good as the testimony of faith, and the hard path as Hell.

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.claim: Giving means giving from one's bounty and fearing God; the good promise is God's compensation, ease is good, and the opposite is withholding wealth, self-sufficiency, denial, and ease toward evil.

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.claim: He said the giver pays God's due, avoids prohibitions, and believes God's promise; the miser withholds that due, feels self-sufficient, and denies the promise.

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r2.claim: He glossed the easy path as Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.claim: Abu Bakr freed weak women who accepted Islam; when his father urged him to free strong protectors instead, he replied that he sought God's reward, and a family member said these verses were revealed about him.

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.claim: The Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Fire is written, but commanded people to act: each is made ready for the deeds of the saved or the wretched, then recited this passage.

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.claim: After the decree in 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds begin anew or are already settled; the Prophet replied to act, since each is made ready for the easy or hard path.

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.claim: Suraqa asked whether deeds were predetermined; the Prophet affirmed the decree but urged action, since each person is eased toward what he was created for, then recited the passage.

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.speaker: بشير بن كعب الأسلمي
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.claim: Asked about deeds, he reports the Prophet answering that they follow the written decree, yet people must act because each is eased toward what he was created for; he recited these verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.claim: Abu Qahafa urged freeing strong men who could protect Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr said he sought God's face, and the report says the passage through ‘he will be satisfied’ was revealed about him.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#4/r1.claim: God prepares the giver for the trait that leads to ease and comfort, such as Paradise and its preliminaries; “easiest” is used through metaphor, metonymy, or figurative attribution.

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r2.claim: Yusrā is the easiest path to comfort and happiness, including easy reckoning and entry into Paradise.

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r3.speaker: مفسّرین
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r3.claim: Exegetes explain taysīr as preparing and making ready, by analogy with fitting a horse with bridle and saddle for riding.

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r4.claim: For one who trusts the promise, the good path that is difficult for others becomes easy to undertake joyfully, and good deeds multiply the means of reaching the goal.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:7/r1.claim: One whom God makes easy for the good path has arrived in this life with gentleness and lives in ease that radiates outward, including calm success in large and small matters.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:7/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:7/r2.claim: This is the promised degree expressed to the Messenger as being made easy for the easy path.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r1.claim: Taysir makes something easy to obtain; its direct object is what is made easy, while the following li- phrase names the beneficiary, as in the cited verses.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r10.claim: One solution keeps facilitate literal and treats the construction as rhetorical inversion: the original sense is making the easy or hard path easy for the person, with inversion intensifying the facilitation.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r11.claim: The inversion is compared with the Arabic expression about presenting a she-camel to a watering trough.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r12.claim: A second solution uses facilitate figuratively for preparation; li- is causal, and al-yusra and al-usra denote Paradise and Hell, with entry understood after the preposition.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r13.claim: On the preparation interpretation, making entry quick is likened to making a difficult thing easy, since difficulty is associated with delay and ease with speed; the cited verse uses easy in the sense of quick.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r14.claim: The same reading makes facilitation follow the acts already produced by giving, restraint, affirmation, or denial, and therefore concerns continuing those acts or increasing them.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r15.claim: A further possibility keeps facilitation literal without inversion: al-yusra and al-usra describe the corresponding conditions, and facilitation means persisting in the deed.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r16.speaker: علي
IBNASHUR:92:7/r16.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ali reports that at a funeral in Baqi al-Gharqad the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether they should rely on that, he commanded them to work, since each person is eased toward the deeds for which they were created, then recited these verses.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r17.claim: The hadith's opening statement about each person's written destination is not the verse's subject: writing represents God's exact prior knowledge of what each person will do.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r18.claim: The question about work is answered by treating righteous action as an indicator of a good end; mention of bad action completes the account rather than answering the question.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r19.claim: The verse connects to the Prophet's words because he recited it as explanation and evidence, especially the clause that God will facilitate; it shows that God enables people toward felicity or misery.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r2.claim: Al-yusra means what is free of hardship, construed as the easy condition of afterlife bliss or as an easy rank or place; more broadly it covers anything beneficial and agreeable.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r20.claim: Alternatively, the verse supports the command to work: deeds mark divine facilitation, with al-yusra signifying happiness and Paradise and al-usra misery and Hell.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r21.claim: The relative clauses describing those who give, are mindful, and affirm indicate that facilitation is caused by their deeds and rewards them by sustaining those deeds; al-yusra praises the deeds as divinely facilitated, as in al-A'la.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r22.claim: The hadith distinguishes God's prior knowledge of human deeds from His address through religious law; deeds are signs of what God knew and means of reaching Paradise or Hell.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r23.claim: Giving is named even though it is included in piety, and miserliness despite being included in self-sufficiency, to encourage Muslims to give; giving, piety, and faith mark Muslims, with their opposites marking polytheists.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r24.claim: The verse uses the rhetorical figures of combination with division and antithesis, with four paired oppositions: giving and stinginess, piety and self-sufficiency, affirmation and denial, and ease and hardship.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم ومجاهد
IBNASHUR:92:7/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and Mujahid interpret al-yusra as Paradise.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r4.claim: Al-usra can mean the condition of hardship, namely punishment, or the place of hardship, namely Hell, as reinforced by the cited description of a hard day for disbelievers.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:92:7/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains facilitation as leading a person through the acts of felicity or misery; easy deeds are good because of their outcome, and difficult deeds are sins by their outcome.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r6.claim: On Ibn Atiyya's interpretation, the feminine forms describe categories of deeds according to their consequences.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r7.claim: On this reading, the future particle sa- signals continued facilitation from now through the end of life, as in the cited verse.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r8.claim: The definite article on al-yusra and al-usra may be generic or referential, depending on the interpretation.

IBNASHUR:92:7/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:7/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:7/r9.claim: The syntax seems reversed: the person is the direct object of facilitate while the easy or hard path is attached by li-, although the person does not benefit from ease in reaching either path.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.claim: The omitted object of اتقى is understood as God; giving, piety, and belief are marks of faith, so the phrase means a believer, as in the disbelievers' admission that they did not pray or feed the poor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.claim: Taysīr means making something easy to obtain; the direct object is what becomes easy, while the following prepositional phrase identifies the beneficiary, as in the cited verses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r1.claim: اليسرى can mean an easy state of bliss in the hereafter or the place of Paradise; Zayd ibn Aslam and Mujāhid are reported to gloss it as Paradise, while the word can broadly mean what benefits without hardship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.claim: He explains facilitation as leading people into acts of happiness or misery: righteous acts are called easy and evil acts hard according to their eventual outcome for the person.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.claim: The future marker can signal continuation from now to life's end, and the definite articles in اليسرى and العسرى may mark a kind or something already known.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.claim: Because the syntax makes the person the one facilitated and the easy or hard outcome the beneficiary, two analyses are possible; the first preserves the literal verb through rhetorical inversion, intensifying the facilitation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.claim: The second analysis uses تيسير figuratively for preparation and uses the لام for purpose: God prepares people for Paradise or Hell, understood as proper names, by hastening their entry; the phrase for Hell is a mocking parallel to the one for Paradise.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.claim: Since the described acts precede the promised facilitation, it refers to continuing and increasing those established deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.claim: Another reading keeps the verb literal and treats easy and difficult as descriptions of a state; facilitation means persisting in action, supported by the Bukhārī report that each person is facilitated toward the work for which they were created and the Prophet then recited these verses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.claim: The hadith's opening statement that each person's destination was written is not the point of these verses; writing represents God's exact knowledge, and the question about whether to rely on that knowledge is answered by saying good deeds signal a good end.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.claim: The verse is connected to the Prophet's recitation as an explanation of فسنيسره: God enables a person to do works of felicity or misery, whether foundational faith or further deeds, and either sense supports divine facilitation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.claim: Alternatively, the recitation supports the command to act: deeds mark the person's facilitation, with easy outcomes meaning felicity and Paradise and difficult outcomes meaning misery and the Fire.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.claim: The relative clause describing the giver and God-fearing person signals that facilitation is caused by those deeds and rewards them by enabling persistence; calling their deeds easy praises them, as in al-Aʿlā.

TABATABAI:92:2-7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r8.claim: Making the person ready for the ease-filled afterlife and Paradise through righteous deeds fits the Qur'an's promises better than merely making good works easier to perform.

ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n4/r1.claim: Asad points to note 6 on 87:8 for this phrase.

BINTSHATI:v2p108/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r1.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r1.claim: Exegetes explain making the way easy as preparing the state most convenient for the one who affirms the good, in this life and the next.

BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the paths are called easy and hard for their outcomes, or they mean the routes to Paradise and Hell.

BINTSHATI:v2p108/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r3.claim: God's promise to make the easy way accessible appears with yusra only in al-Ala 87:8 and here, for the Prophet and for the giver who is mindful and affirms the good.

BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.claim: Unlike the verbal nouns usr and yusr, usra and yusra convey the extreme of hardship or ease, as do Quranic forms such as the greatest seizure and the greatest Fire.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.claim: The first antithesis pairs virtue and vice catalogues with promises of their eschatological outcomes; first-person plural marks these promises as God's speech and authorizes them alongside the oath.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.claim: The destinations are initially veiled through the near-homophonous opposites yusr and ʿusr combined with yassara, making the damned person's promised ease rhetorically paradoxical.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.claim: The first stanza is symmetrical, with matching behavior-to-consequence sequences and a cross-rhyme produced by vowel variation, as Neuwirth observes.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.claim: The two halves are linked by paired terms: giving versus stinginess, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.claim: The opposition between ease and hardship parallels 94:5–6, while the promise in 87:8 addresses the messenger.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.claim: Verses 5–7 describe the character and belief that qualify a person for success in the Hereafter and ease the way to it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r3.claim: Al-yusrā also suppresses a noun such as al-ʿāqibah; God helps the virtuous by removing obstacles and strengthening their desire to continue, as at 29:69.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r4.claim: The destination is called al-yusrā because the reckoning is easy, as described at 84:7–8.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.claim: The virtuous fight their base desires at every step and grow stronger through that struggle, eventually reaching the servants’ company and Paradise described at 89:29–30.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r6.claim: Yusra means the easiest path of ease and happiness, and can also mean a greater capacity or virtue for doing good.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r7.claim: As a person tries to do good, God strengthens that will and eases good deeds until generosity becomes a stable character trait.

QIRAAT-ER:92:7:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:92:7:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:92:7:2#1/r1.claim: Adding a short vowel between sīn and rāʾ is phonological and does not affect root or meaning.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.claim: Ease and hardship may occur in this life or the next, both of which belong to God; people should therefore follow what He commands.

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet taught each person's destination is recorded, then urged action because everyone is eased toward what they were created for; he recited these verses.

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that God makes the way to obedience amiable and grants success until obedience becomes easiest, like God's expanding a guided person's breast for submission.

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r7.claim: Ease is linked to God's desire for ease rather than hardship and to reverence, through which God appoints ease in one's affairs.
